raw_answer_text:
A1: The switch learns from the source address of every frame it receives, since the flow shows wire → learn → lookup, meaning learning happens before and independent of the destination lookup/forwarding outcome.
A2: It associates the source MAC address (SA) with the ingress port.
A3: Whether the destination MAC address is found as a single entry in the MAC table (a "hit") determines forwarding to one port; if not found, the switch floods.
A4: The switch floods the frame to every port in the VLAN; the ingress port is always excluded.
A5: NOT STATED
A6: A switch filters (discards) a frame when the entry is found in the table and the looked-up egress port is the same as the ingress port.
A7: NOT STATED beyond the general rule: before learning, the "hit" decision is "no" so the frame is flooded to all ports except ingress; once learned, the "hit" is "yes" and the frame is forwarded to the single learned port instead (unless that port equals the ingress port, in which case it is filtered).
A8: NOT STATED
